applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Statics and structural-analysis fundamentals from public educational sources; not a foundation or connection design check.

source_refs.locator: Types of Supports and Their Characteristics
Supports, support modelling and DOF notation

claims.text: Support reactions are consequences of restrained or prescribed degrees of freedom, not arbitrary arrows added after analysis.

source_refs.locator: Pin, roller, link, and fixed support descriptions

claims.text: Named support types such as pin, roller, link, and fixed support are shorthand for different translation and rotation restraint assumptions.
Reaction signs must be interpreted with the selected coordinate frame and assumed positive direction before they are treated as physical problems such as uplift or missing restraint.

limitations: This card covers idealised support behaviour, not real bearing, footing, base-plate, bolt, or soil capacity.
Unilateral, settlement, spring, or nonlinear support behaviour needs separate modelling rules.

pages_used: Types of Supports and Their Characteristics

summary: Fraia should represent named supports as explicit restrained or prescribed DOFs so reactions, signs, and physical assumptions remain inspectable.
title: Support Reactions and Idealisation
